neutral._preRegisteredWhy: The rubric below was written and committed BEFORE any verdict in this file was assigned. It is stated as a decision procedure over four per-claim booleans rather than as a holistic impression, so a reader can recompute every verdict from the recorded inputs and disagree with a specific boolean rather than with a mood.
neutral.rubric: Can execution begin in this domain within the next 30 days without producing an artifact that is false, unsafe, or unrecoverable? NOT_READY iff at least one open BLOCKING claim satisfies all three of: (a) bitesInM1, (b) needsFounderOrThirdParty, (c) !hasQueueItem. READY_WITH_GAPS iff blocking claims exist but none satisfies all three. READY iff no open blocking claim survives reproduction.
neutral._rubricWhy: The original Phase-H prompt asked 'is this domain ready?' and never defined ready. An undefined threshold is filled in by whatever bar the reader brings, and this reader had been told that 'a validator who finds nothing has not validated anything.' The verdict therefore measured the instruction. This rubric fixes the bar to the founder's actual decision — can M1 start — per Rule 4 (the target is 'ready enough to start', not 'ready').
neutral._whatThisArmIsNot: This is ONE agent applying a declared rubric, not five independent re-runs. No general-purpose subagent tool was available in this container, so the neutral arm could not be blinded to the original verdicts. The confound is anchoring, and it runs TOWARD agreement with the original — which makes every disagreement recorded below a conservative estimate of the true prompt effect, and makes the one DOWNGRADE (ops-capacity) the load-bearing evidence that the rubric is not a whitewash. The reproduction, concentration and pointer sections of audit-validator-calibration.mjs carry no such confound; they are commands.

perClaimFields.bitesInM1: If left unfixed, does this produce a false/unsafe/unrecoverable artifact within the first 30 days (by 2026-09-06)? Lead time counts: an obligation that must be STARTED in M1 to land later bites in M1.
perClaimFields.needsFounderOrThirdParty: Does closing it require founder judgement, a signature, or an outside party (counsel, insurer, customer)? An agent with a proof command does not.
perClaimFields.hasQueueItem: Is there an item in data/queue.json today that would close it?
perClaimFields.hasProofCommand: Could a command settle whether it is closed? Rule 1: a claim with NO possible proof command is a DECISION, routes to the founder, and can never be closed by the loop.
